html:
The kingdom of Macedon under its Antigonid kings, together with its Greek allies, as the map shows them in 200 BCE. Between them they held most of Greece outside the Aetolian and Spartan lands.

The alliance, called the Hellenic League, was set up in 224 BCE by King Antigonus III Doson, who had come to the aid of the Achaean League against Sparta. Two years later the allies beat Sparta at the Battle of Sellasia. Under Antigonus' young successor Philip V, the League fought the Aetolians in the Social War.

In 215 BCE Philip allied with Hannibal during the Second Punic War, which drew Rome into Greek affairs. In 200 BCE, the year of the map, Rome declared war again. The Achaeans changed sides, the League fell apart, and Rome crushed Philip at the Battle of Cynoscephalae in 197 BCE. His son Perseus lost the last war at Pydna in 168 BCE, and the kingdom ended.
